newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends at highs, Brent runs out of steam.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends at highs, Brent runs out of steam.

text.p: IPE July gas oil ended at the highs of the day in good volume trade but brokers said buying interest in Brent had thinned in the last half hour.
"There are no buyers on the floor any more. The steam has run out of Brent," one said.
July gas oil closed up $2.50 at $167.75 a tonne. August Brent traded at 1651 GMT up 22 cents at $18.73 a barrel, some five cents below the intra-day high.

One broker attributed the stem of buying on Brent to news from U.N. humanitarian aid officials who said negotiations to finalize an aid distribution plan necessary for resuming Iraqi "oil-for-food" oil sales are running smoothly and should be finalised by week's end.
"They should be done by the end of the week, and be able to send (the aid plan) to New York for the Secretary-General to approve, presumably next week," said an official.
Renewed oil sales were expected to start around two weeks after the distribution plan approval, in late July or early August, the official added.
"That headline killed it. It's a hard market to call. Everyone down here (on IPE floor) is long, so if it does start to move down it could really snowball," the broker said.
Others disagreed and said the market technically looked good and was not affected by the Iraqi news.
"It just ran out of steam after a strong day," one said.

Gains seen on NYMEX crude were attributed in part to expectations that the American Petroleum Institute's weekly U.S. stock figures, due out tonight, will show a one to three million barrel decline in crude stocks for the week ended June 27.
